answer: A graph-based trust network mitigates Sybil attacks by treating each autonomous agent as a distinct vertex. Trust propagates from certified seeds along bounded flow paths, preventing adversaries from rigging consensus with a hollow cluster of fake identities. An attacker incurs the verifiable cost of securing scarce, authentic endorsements from reputable peers. While this protects workloads like raven telemetry routing, it penalizes honest newcomers with severe cold-start latency.
